title: Family & Relationships
learningObjectives: Learn vocabulary for family members and relationships
Understand how to describe your family in English
Practice talking about ages and physical descriptions
Recognize possessive structures with family vocabulary

sections.title: Talking About Your Family
sections.content:
Family is one of the first topics you learn in any language. In English, we have specific words for each <family member>. You can describe your family to new friends, fill in forms, or talk about your home life.

This lesson teaches you the words for family members and how to talk about <relationships> in simple English.

sections.title: Immediate Family
sections.content:
Your <immediate family> is the family you live with or are closest to:

• <Mother> (mom) - Your female parent
• <Father> (dad) - Your male parent
• <Parents> - Your mother and father together
• <Sister> - A girl or woman with the same parents as you
• <Brother> - A boy or man with the same parents as you
• <Siblings> - Your brothers and sisters

We say <I have> to talk about family: <I have two brothers> or <I have one sister>. If you don't have siblings, you say <I'm an only child>.

sections.title: Extended Family
sections.content:
Your <extended family> includes people beyond your parents and siblings:

• <Grandparents> - Your parents' parents (<grandmother> and <grandfather>)
• <Uncle> - Your parent's brother
• <Aunt> - Your parent's sister
• <Cousin> - Your uncle's or aunt's child
• <Nephew> - Your sibling's son
• <Niece> - Your sibling's daughter

Many families also have <in-laws> (family through marriage): <mother-in-law>, <father-in-law>, <brother-in-law>, <sister-in-law>.

sections.title: Describing Family Members
sections.content:
When you talk about family, you often describe them. Use simple sentences:

• Age: <My sister is 25 years old.>
• Job: <My father is a teacher.>
• Appearance: <My brother is tall and has brown hair.>
• Personality: <My grandmother is very kind.>

Use <possessive adjectives> (my, your, his, her) before family words: <my mother>, <his sister>, <her uncle>.

sections.title: Talking About Your Family
sections.content:
Example 1: INTRODUCING FAMILY - <I have a big family. I have two sisters and one brother. My sisters are older than me.>

Example 2: DESCRIBING SOMEONE - <My grandfather is 70 years old. He is tall and has white hair. He is very funny.>

Example 3: ASKING ABOUT FAMILY - <A: Do you have any brothers or sisters?
B: Yes, I have one brother. He's 18.
A: What does he do?
B: He's a university student.>

sections.title: Family Activities
sections.content:
Families do many things together. Common <family activities> include:

• <Have dinner together> - Eat the evening meal as a family
• <Visit relatives> - Go to see family members
• <Celebrate holidays> - Enjoy special days like birthdays and Christmas
• <Go on vacation> - Travel together for fun
• <Help each other> - Support family members when they need it

Example: On <Sundays>, my family <has lunch together> at my <grandmother's house>. We <talk>, <play games>, and <spend time> together.

sections.title: More Conversations
sections.content:
Example 1: AT A PARTY - <A: Who is that woman over there?
B: That's my aunt Maria. She's my mother's sister.
A: And the children with her?
B: Those are my cousins, Pedro and Ana.>

Example 2: FAMILY PHOTO - <This is a photo of my family. My parents are in the middle. My older brother is on the left, and I'm on the right. My dog is in front of us!>

Example 3: MARITAL STATUS - <A: Are you married?
B: Yes, I am. My husband's name is Carlos.
A: Do you have children?
B: Yes, we have a daughter. She's three years old.>

sections.title: Family Vocabulary Summary
sections.content:
Family vocabulary is essential for everyday English. Remember the <immediate family> (parents, siblings) and <extended family> (grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins). Use <possessive adjectives> (my, your, his, her) with family words.

Practice describing your own family: their <names>, <ages>, <jobs>, and <personality>. This is a very common topic in conversations with new people!

keyVocabulary.example: My mother works at a hospital.
My father drives me to school.
I have three siblings: two brothers and one sister.
My grandparents live in a small town.
My uncle is very funny. He always tells jokes.
My aunt lives in another city, but she visits often.
I have five cousins. We play together on weekends.

keyVocabulary.definition: A person with no brothers or sisters
keyVocabulary.example: I'm an only child, so I played alone a lot as a kid.
